newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian brokerage's shares surge on takeover talk.
newsitem.headline: Canadian brokerage's shares surge on takeover talk.

text.p: Midland Walwyn Inc. shares shot higher on Wednesday after a shareholder rights group faxed several news organizations a letter saying a U.S. brokerage was interested in buying Canada's last major independent broker.
But officials at Midland and its rumored suitor, U.S. brokerage Smith Barney, denied the legitimacy of the document.
Midland shares surged to a 52-week high of C$13.95 before pulling back to trade up C85 cents at C$13 on the Toronto Stock Exchange.

Midland said it did not regard the letter, addressed to its chief executive Robert Schultz from Canadian Alliance of Individual Investors Executive Director Stephen Handler, as a genuine offer for the company.
"We have I believe probably the same letter that you do and it's our view that it's not a bona fide offer," Brad Doney, general counsel for Midland, told Reuters.
The letter said an anonymous U.S. financial services house was interested in acquiring Midland in a deal that would give shareholders about C$15 ($11.10) a share.
"The acquirer who wishes to remain anonymous at the moment does not wish to launch a hostile takeover bid for MWI," the letter said.
Handler told Reuters the U.S. brokerage was Smith Barney, a unit of Travelers Group Inc.
Smith Barney said there was no basis for the report.
"I can absolutely deny this," Smith Barney spokesman Bob Connor said.

James Hunter, chief operating officer of Canadian fund manager Mackenzie Financial Inc., which has a 20 percent stake in Midland, said it had not been approached by any U.S. investors or institutions."

Takeover speculation about Midland, whose Midland Walwyn Capital is the last major Canadian brokerage not yet affiliated with a bank, has persisted since Royal Bank of Canada last year acquired Richardson Greenshields of Canada Ltd., the country's only other big independent dealer.
Doney said Midland wanted to remain independent.
Last October, Schultz said the brokerage was not for sale and suggested the probability of a hostile takeover bid was low.
